title: Redwood July 2026 All-Hands
summary: Leadership reviewed Q2 performance (ARR growth, latency improvements), announced a tighter roadmap for the serving runtime and Dedicated capacity, confirmed Private deployment milestones and SOC 2 re-audit timeline. Action items include a pricing readout for Dedicated customers, an engineering deep-dive to finalize kernel-selection benchmarks, and a security packet update for enterprise prospects. The all-hands closed with Q&A and hiring priorities for Q3.

Samir to follow up on top 5 enterprise renewals and schedule EBRs

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Start time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: 1:15
Attendees: Aisha Patel (CEO), Ethan Ross (CTO), Jordan Lee (Head of GTM), Priya Natarajan (SE), Carlos Mendes (Product), Maya Chen (VP Eng), Samir Rao (Head Sales), Lena Ortiz (Security), Jules Park (Finance)

Summary: see above

00:00:00 - Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, welcome to the July all-hands. Appreciate you all making time, we have a packed agenda, Q2 recap, product updates, security, hiring. We'll start with Aisha for a few words.

00:00:32 - Aisha Patel: Morning team. Quick thank you — Q2 was strong, ARR up 18% quarter over quarter, churn held steady at 1.8%. We still have work on margin profile, the optimize toolkit is starting to show up in customer conversations which is great. We'll be tightening priorities this quarter.

00:01:05 - Ethan Ross: Quick note from infra: latency p95 for hosted API dropped from 220ms to 170ms for 512 token workflows after the recent kernel selection tweaks. That's with the new continuous batching and a few quantization-path optimizations. There's still edge cases for KV cache heavy workloads that we need to patch.

00:01:38 - Priya Natarajan: yeah the KV cash, uh cache, sorry, the KV cache pathology shows up when you have a lot of mixed seq lengths. We have two fixes in staging, one is better prefix batching and the other is a micro-op that avoids extra copies on the quantized path.

00:02:12 - Maya Chen: are we seeing regressions for embeddings customers when we apply aggressive quant? We had a support ticket last week where semantics were slightly off for reranking.

00:02:30 - Priya Natarajan: good callout, we saw a small delta on one model at very low temp settings. We're adding a validation gate in the compilation step: if semantic embedding drift > threshold we'll fallback to a higher-precision kernel. It's not a universal setting, it's per-model/per-workload.

00:03:02 - Carlos Mendes: product update — roadmap highlight is Dedicated 2.0: more predictable autoscaling, burst capacity for seasonal loads, and better metrics export to our console. We'll run a canary with two customers in Aug.

00:03:24 - Samir Rao: great — push sales collateral early. We need concrete examples of throughput vs price for finance and healthcare customers.

00:03:40 - Jules Park: on pricing, finance wants to float a few scenarios; can we get burn-down of unit economics per-token for held capacity vs burst?

00:03:55 - Carlos Mendes: yes, we'll produce a pricing matrix. I'll own that.

00:04:10 - Aisha Patel: security update, Lena?

00:04:18 - Lena Ortiz: SOC 2 re-audit kicked off, auditor doing initial scoping next week. We also have the KMS/HSM integration roadmap: MFA for key rotation, customer-managed keys for Private deployments. Need to update the security packet for sales and renewals — there are questions from large prospects about key residency and audit logs.

00:04:46 - Jordan Lee: can we have an exec summary security one-pager for sales by early Aug? Last renewal call flagged missing details.

00:04:55 - Lena Ortiz: yes, I'll publish by 2026-08-10.

00:05:10 - Ethan Ross: technical deep dive scheduled next Tuesday — Priya will run kernel selection benchmarks and show perf/accuracy tradeoffs across quant and fp16. This will shape the Dedicated default profiles.

00:05:28 - Priya Natarajan: note — benchmarks are noisy. We'll include variance and tail latency. I'll share the spreadsheet with execs and product by Monday.

00:05:45 - Maya Chen: ops question — for Private we had a customer ask about on-prem air-gapped installs and uptime SLOs. Where are we on install docs and runbooks?

00:05:59 - Ethan Ross: we're finalizing the on-prem installer and the init scripts. Ops team has a runbook draft; aim to get official doc set before the first pilot in late Aug. There will be an internal verification checklist for network/SAN and KMS.

00:06:25 - Jordan Lee: Customer highlight — Beacon Health pilot is in POC, their security team asked for end-to-end encryption and audit logs. Samir is coordinating.

00:06:40 - Samir Rao: Beacon Health is moving to a private deployment for PHI compliance. Key asks: SSO/SAML integration, role-based access controls, and detailed audit logs. They also wanted example SLA language for latency-critical workflows.

00:06:58 - Lena Ortiz: SSO is mostly ready; RBAC model needs minor tweaks for their roles. Audit logging is available but we need to document retention options and export formats.

00:07:20 - Carlos Mendes: product note — we need a template SLA that differentiates host tiers: hosted best-effort, dedicated backed SLA, private customer SLA. Jules, finance needs to model that.

00:07:36 - Jules Park: ok will do. Also headcount update?

00:07:43 - Aisha Patel: we're approving 12 roles this quarter — infra, SRE, and two go-to-market. Hiring velocity needs to be faster but targeted. Recruiting will reach out with bar-raise profiles.

00:08:02 - Audience Q&A starts (open mic)

00:08:12 - Staff member (unlabeled): question about Optimize — any new auto-tuning for batching thresholds?

00:08:25 - Priya Natarajan: yes, Optimize will propose batching and cache configs by analyzing request histograms. We're adding a simulation mode so customers can see cost/latency impact before applying.

00:08:45 - Staff member: will that be available for Dedicated?

00:08:52 - Priya Natarajan: initial release for hosted, but Dedicated integration is planned for Q4.

00:09:05 - Jordan Lee: Sales spotlight — we closed a strategic deal with a payments company, onboarding in Sept, will use Dedicated with burst capacity. Good reference for fintech.

00:09:22 - Samir Rao: on renewals — there are three mid-market renewals where we need to present Dedicated options; follow-ups will be scheduled this week.

00:09:40 - Aisha Patel: leadership reflection: stay focused on reliability and predictable economics. Open models will keep moving, our value prop is serving and predictable SLOs.

00:09:58 - Ethan Ross: tech note — kernel selector will default to the most stable kernel for a given seq distribution; we'll expose override flags for power users. Also working on a more robust fallback when memory blowup is detected.

00:10:20 - Priya Natarajan: anecdote: we had a customer run a long chat which triggered a KV cache eviction bug — turned out to be an edge-case in the redistribution logic. Fixed in canary. Shows need for stronger chaos tests.

00:10:45 - Carlos Mendes: mobile SDK progress — we shipped an initial SDK to partners; next step is a security review to ensure token handling is safe.

00:11:01 - Lena Ortiz: token handling review planned; we'll include guidance on short-lived tokens and refresh patterns.

00:11:18 - Jordan Lee: Marketing update (Samir and marketing team) — new case studies incoming, bench-slide deck updated with latency/cost graphs — please use conservatively in sales until we finalize the validation notes.

00:11:40 - Samir Rao: early feedback from a retail customer shows 22% unit cost decrease after enabling prefix caching and optimized kernels. We'll validate across more customers.

00:11:58 - Audience question: any update on marketplace listings?

00:12:06 - Jordan Lee: we're in late-stage review with two cloud marketplaces; expect listings in Q3. This will help reach regulated customers via partner channels.

00:12:22 - Aisha Patel: quick org note — leadership will run skip-levels next week. Also reminder on the company-wide offsite in Sept.

00:12:33 - Staff member: will offsite include customer deep-dive sessions?

00:12:38 - Aisha Patel: yes, we'll have product/customer panels.

00:12:50 - Carlos Mendes: back to Dedicated pricing — we need to present three tiers: Reserved (committed), Burst (reserved + burst), Enterprise (private + support). I'll draft examples with throughput and token unit economics.

00:13:12 - Jules Park: finance will need cost models for each tier and expected revenue impact.

00:13:20 - Q&A continues with smaller topics: office moves, remote work policy tweaks, and how we measure uptime credits.

00:14:10 - Technical shoutout: infra team for hitless rollout this month. Ethan thanks the SREs.

00:14:28 - Closing remarks: Aisha summarizes the three top priorities for Q3: 1) Reliability & SLOs (Dedicated+Hosted), 2) Security/compliance (SOC2 + KMS), 3) GTM: ramp Dedicated & Private pilots.

00:14:52 - Jordan Lee: recap of next steps and owners — see action items. We'll follow up with email and set the kernel benchmark deep-dive next Tuesday.

00:15:05 - Meeting ends

Notes on transcription: Some speaker labels may be compressed, occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "KV cash"), timestamps are approximate. There are additional side-channel chats and shared links referenced during the meeting (deck: https://redwood.internal/decks/q2-product-update, kernel benchmarks: internal link to spreadsheet).
